items.followUp: Define isotopes and give the isotopes of hydrogen.

rubric.why: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
rubric.description: Defines isotopes by identifying what is the same and what differs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the shared property and the difference.

rubric.why: The two common isotopes of chlorine have mass numbers 35 and 37.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or writing both chlorine isotopes.

modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
The isotopes of chlorine are chlorine-35 (³⁵Cl) and chlorine-37 (³⁷Cl).

items.followUp: Why are noble gases generally chemically stable?

rubric.why: Noble gases have complete outermost electron shells.
rubric.description: Identifies the complete outermost electron shell of noble gases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that their valence shell is complete.

rubric.why: Their stable electron arrangement gives them little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons.
rubric.description: Explains how the complete shell results in low reactivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting the stable arrangement to little or no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons.

modelAnswer: Noble gases have complete outermost electron shells (helium has a complete duplet; the others have an octet).
This stable arrangement means they have little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons, so they are not reactive.

items.followUp: Explain how shielding affects the removal of an outer-shell electron.

rubric.why: Inner-shell electrons shield outer electrons from the full attraction of the nucleus.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of inner electrons on the nuclear attraction experienced by outer electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding by inner electrons reduces the nuclear attraction on outer electrons.

rubric.why: Reduced attraction makes outer electrons easier to remove, allowing cations to form.
rubric.description: Connects shielding with easy electron removal and cation formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding makes an outer electron easier to remove or a cation easier to form.

modelAnswer: Inner-shell electrons shield the outermost electrons from the full attraction of the nucleus.
The outer electrons are therefore less strongly held and can be removed easily to form a cation.
